ANYPS5 / THE COMPILED FRONTIER

All software
is open source.

The next engineering surface is already compiled. AnyPS5 shows what people and agents can build when source is missing.

Follow one instruction ↘
33,740 stars for the project.2,916 forks of the work.Meet AnyPS5 ↗

Start with
the executable.

PS5 and the target PCs share x86-64. AnyPS5 changes the executable’s format, rebuilds the libraries it calls, and recompiles its shaders. It can also rewrite supported AMD-specific instructions for Intel. Above is a real tested substitution: EXTRQ becomes MOVQ plus NOP padding. [1]

→→→

Same CPU vocabulary. Different executable format, libraries, and operating-system expectations.

One missing call.
Four billion checks.

232possible float bit patterns

Dusklight stopped at cPGyc5FGjy0, a missing libc import. It was atanhf. In merged PR #5036, the author implements it and reports checking all 4,294,967,296 possible 32-bit inputs against the bundled code. The PR explicitly discloses AI assistance. [2]

That is the new engineering conversation: read the binary, recover the behavior, write the replacement, prove what you can. An agent joins the work; the tests still have to answer.

Sources, data & how this was made

GitHub evidence only. Metadata: 13 October 2026, 10:05:27 UTC. Complete captured main history: 6,802 commits, with author-date activity over 72 calendar days. Complete captured PR population: 4,319; merged: 2,518. Accounts identify attribution, not unique people or unaided human labor. The star total is a dated snapshot; star-event dates were inaccessible. These records establish activity and participation, not what caused attention.

Official progress: published 13 October 2026, 10:34:23 UTC, source commit 53aea1f. Library counts include declared exports and can include inert stubs; shader counts measure recognized encodings. These are not game-compatibility scores. The 2³² comparison is the PR author’s report, not a test rerun here. AMD rewriting covers supported static instructions, not every generated instruction.

The binary fixture is a conceptual inspection instrument built with Anatomy (MIT). Its lamps encode actual tested bytes, not PS5 hardware internals. The author field adapts Lieflat’s Hundred Field under its PolyForm Noncommercial license. Lieflat Charts was developed by 躺在废墟里. Official progress SVG reproduced from AnyPS5; upstream credit and license retained. Fonts use SIL OFL. This site is independent of Sony and the project’s maintainers.
